question: Should OpenClaw add a per-target-agent child-run cap, and should its public shape be `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` rather than a broader caller-selected lane API?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but the change adds public configuration and scheduler policy while related reports propose non-equivalent requester, parent-session, foreground-agent, and named-lane scopes.

options.title: Target-agent cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as a target-keyed second gate beneath the existing global subagent cap for native and ACP runs.

options.title: Unified lane design
options.body: Design a broader lane API only if it directly models target resource caps and avoids relying on callers to choose lanes correctly.

options.title: Keep global controls
options.body: Decline a new setting and accept that a resource-constrained target cannot be isolated from other subagent targets.

recommendation.title: Target-agent cap
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as a target-keyed second gate beneath the existing global subagent cap for native and ACP runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The concurrency resolver and shared lane architecture appear to date to their commits, and the issue already has their maintainer-facing follow-up context.
